title: Inverting the Celsius-to-Fahrenheit Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Temperature conversion obeys $F=\frac{9}{5}C+32$. Solve this relation for $C$ as a function of $F$, then use your formula to convert $68^{\circ}$F to degrees Celsius.

steps.title: Undo the Constant Term
steps.explanation: Subtract $32$ from both sides to isolate the term carrying $C$.
steps.why: Solving a linear relation peels operations off in reverse order.

steps.title: Undo the Scaling Factor
steps.explanation: Multiplying by $5/9$, the reciprocal of $9/5$, yields $C$ as a function of $F$.
steps.why: The conversion formulas are inverses of each other because each undoes the other's operations.

steps.title: Convert the Specific Reading
steps.explanation: $68^{\circ}$F corresponds to $20^{\circ}$C, a mild room temperature worth memorizing as a reference point.
steps.why: Substitution into the inverse formula completes the conversion.
